---
name: prop-type-barrier-blocks-consumers
description: A theorem taking a Prop-valued hypothesis's components can be unusable by every consumer holding the bundled class; only elaborating an application finds it
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

I proved a theorem taking the four *components* of a `Prop`-valued bundled
hypothesis (`IsGaloisQuotient`, an `∃`) and concluding a `Type`-valued
`RepresentableBy`. Sorry-free, kernel-clean, all declarations axiom-clean against a
live `sorryAx` control. It was **unusable by every consumer**: `obtain ⟨e, he, heq,
huniv⟩ := hq` fails with "`Exists.casesOn` can only eliminate into `Prop`". Every
per-declaration check passed, because the defect is not in any declaration — it is
in the step from the class a consumer holds to the components I asked for.

**Why:** the whole audit vocabulary (sorry-free, axiom-clean, rooted, non-vacuous,
hypotheses satisfiable) is per-declaration. "Can the caller get from what it holds
to what I take?" is not a property of my declaration, so nothing in that vocabulary
looks at it. See [[axiom-clean-vs-applicable]] — binders satisfiable at a good site
and the application still fails to elaborate — this is the same lesson with a
mechanism attached, and the mechanism is universe/sort, not instances.

**How to apply:** after landing a theorem, write the application a consumer would
write and elaborate it. Not `#check` of the theorem — an `example` that starts from
the *bundled* hypothesis and ends at the conclusion. If the destructuring fails,
land the `Nonempty`/choice-mediated form yourself rather than leaving it. Useful
asymmetry once found: an existential *conclusion* needs no choice (eliminating `∃`
into `Prop` is fine), so the same reduction stated at the `∃`-shaped consumer
interface is choice-free while the data-valued one is not — ship both.

Related: [[finish-it-instead-of-pricing-it]] (the fix was 20 minutes),
[[witness-is-not-producer]].
